tb21_profile.skill: Craft one source file that two different compilers' lexers/parsers each accept, by exploiting comment, preprocessor and token-level divergences, while both produce the same numeric output
tb21_profile.domain: Rust (rustc 1.75) and C++ (g++ 13) toolchains; language grammar/preprocessor corners, systems compilation
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec / adversarial puzzle: one small artifact, two exact build+run invocations, exact stdout

notes: CalibForge is decisively the best pool here and by a wide margin - it contains six genuine single-file polyglot tasks, all graded strong, one of which (20260617_210354_017) is essentially this TB2.1 task with bash added. Nothing in the v1 pool has a single-file polyglot at all; TMax's 77 'polyglot' hits are all multi-language build-orchestration projects, a lexical false positive on the word. Terminal-Lego contributed exactly one real polyglot (task_00979, bash/batch) and otherwise only Fibonacci/Rust-tutorial filler; both new corpora beat the old ones here. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has nothing defensible: its top hits are ~15 near-identical Rust guessing games, and I fell back to g++-version-gated C++ and ARM64 assembly implement-and-build tasks, all scoring 1-2 and all 'absent' verifier. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench likewise have no real candidate above overall 3; ranks 7-10 in both are honest filler. FREE candidates excluded from final_top10 and from per_source where I had better options: TMax task_009068_ceebc4fa, task_006408_a7697452, task_000113_5f736d5a, task_005057_1c2c3881 and TerminalWorld tw_143212, tw_362046, tw_138882 were all dropped for being FREE despite decent retrieval rank.
